- URL: `/about-coaching/`
- Title: About CSMP IAS Coaching in Lucknow | Trusted UPSC/PCS Institute
- Meta description: Know about CSMP IAS Coaching in Lucknow – a trusted UPSC coaching institute in Gomti Nagar known for quality teaching, guidance, and results.
- H1: About Coaching
- Body:

```
About Coaching
About CSMP IAS Coaching in Lucknow
CSMP IAS Lucknow is a premier Civil Services coaching institute dedicated to preparing aspirants for the UPSC Civil Services Examination (IAS, IPS, IFS) and State PCS exams. Our focus is not only on completing the syllabus but on developing exam-oriented thinking, analytical ability, and administrative aptitude required to succeed in competitive examinations.
Located in the academic hub of Lucknow, CSMP IAS has earned the trust of students through its quality teaching, disciplined learning environment, and personalized mentorship system.
Mission and vision
At CSMP IAS, our vision is to develop honest and capable civil servants for the nation. Our mission is to provide clear concepts, personal guidance, and exam-focused preparation, with special attention to current affairs, answer writing, and building confidence among UPSC and PCS aspirants.
Search your program
Undergraduate programs
Graduate programs
CSMP IAS
Why Choose CSMP IAS Lucknow?
CSMP IAS Lucknow is chosen for its experienced faculty, exam-focused teaching, updated study material, and personal mentoring. We provide a disciplined learning environment that helps UPSC and PCS aspirants prepare with clarity, confidence, and the right strategy.
Experienced & Dedicated Faculty
Comprehensive Course Structure
Updated & Exam-Oriented Study Material
Personal Mentorship & Doubt Resolution
Regular Test Series & Evaluation
Features
Prelims Test Series
Mains Answer Writing Practice
Solved Model Answers
Daily current affairs analysis
Student-Centric Learning Environment
CSMP IAS Lucknow provides a disciplined, focused, and positive learning environment where students can prepare effectively without unnecessary pressure. With small batch sizes, students receive better interaction and personal attention, along with continuous study support and guidance. Regular motivation and strategy sessions help students stay focused, confident, and on the right path throughout their preparation journey.
Location Advantage – IAS Coaching in Lucknow
CSMP IAS Lucknow provides a disciplined, focused, and positive learning environment where students can prepare effectively without unnecessary pressure. With small batch sizes, students receive better interaction and personal attention, along with continuous study support and guidance. Regular motivation and strategy sessions help students stay focused, confident, and on the right path throughout their preparation journey.
```

Preparation Tips
Mentorship & Support
Where is CSMP IAS coaching located in Lucknow?
We are located in the heart of Gomti Nagar, near the main market. Our center is easy to reach by auto, tempo, or metro. Visit us at
3/186, Vivek Khand 2, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh 226010
.
Which is the best IAS coaching in Gomti Nagar?
CSMP IAS is rated as the best IAS coaching in Gomti Nagar because of our personal mentorship, small batch size (50 students), and experienced teachers from Delhi.
Is Gomti Nagar a good place for UPSC preparation?
Yes! Gomti Nagar is a peaceful and safe area for students. It has many libraries, bookstores, and good hostels nearby, making it perfect for serious studies.
How can I book a free demo class?
You can book a free demo class by calling us at
+91 8887039761
or filling out the form on this website. You can also reach us on WhatsApp at the same number. Come and sit in a real class to see how we teach.
Do you offer online classes for students outside Lucknow?
Yes, we have a hybrid model. If you cannot come to Gomti Nagar, you can watch live classes on our App from your home.
What are the office timings for admission?
Our admission office in Gomti Nagar is open from 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, Monday to Sunday. For queries, you can email us at
contact@csmpias.com
.
Is there a hostel facility near the coaching center?
Yes, there are many safe and affordable hostels and PGs for boys and girls within 500 meters of our Gomti Nagar center. Our team will help you find a room.
Can I speak to a teacher before joining?
Yes, we allow you to meet our senior mentors before paying fees. We believe in transparency. Feel free to contact us at
+91 8887039761
or email
contact@csmpias.com
to schedule a meeting.
What subjects are covered in the GS Foundation Course?
We cover everything: History, Geography, Polity, Economy, Environment, Science & Tech, Ethics, and Essay. We also include CSAT coaching.
Do you provide coaching for CSAT?
Yes, CSAT is part of our full course. We teach Math, Reasoning, and English from the basics so that even Arts students can pass easily.
What is the duration of the IAS course?
The complete foundation course takes 10 to 12 months. Classes are held 5 to 6 days a week.
Do you provide printed study material?
Yes, every student gets a set of 12 printed books and monthly current affairs magazines. You do not need to buy extra books from the market.
What is the batch size at CSMP Lucknow?
We strictly keep only 50 students per batch. This ensures that the teacher can focus on every single student.
If I miss a class, how can I cover it?
Don't worry. All offline classes are recorded. You will get access to the video on our Student App for revision.
Do you conduct current affairs classes?
Yes, we have a special Current Affairs class every weekend to cover news from The Hindu and Indian Express newspapers.
Is this course for Prelims or Mains?
It is an Integrated Course. We prepare you for both Prelims and Mains together because the syllabus is connected.
What is the fee for IAS coaching in Lucknow?
To know the current fee structure for the GS Foundation Course, please contact our admission counseling team directly. You can call or WhatsApp us at
+91 8887039761
or email
contact@csmpias.com
.
Can I pay the fee in installments (EMI)?
Yes, we offer an easy installment plan. Please reach out to our administration office at
+91 8887039761
to understand the payment schedule and EMI options.
Do you offer any scholarships?
Yes, we conduct a Scholarship Test every Sunday. You can avail a scholarship on your tuition fees based on your performance in the test.
Is the study material fee included?
Yes, the course fee is comprehensive and includes all books, notes, bag, and test series. There are absolutely no hidden charges.
Is there a discount for one-time payment?
Yes, if you pay the full amount at the time of admission, you are eligible for a special discount. Please contact the front desk for details.
Do I get a refund if I leave the course?
We have a transparent refund policy for the initial days of the course. Please read our admission form or contact our office for specific terms and conditions.
Is the test series charged separately?
No, the Class Test Series (Weekly Prelims + Fortnightly Mains) is completely free for our classroom students.
Do you have special discounts for female students?
Yes, to support girl child education, we offer an additional discount for female aspirants. Please inquire at the time of admission.
I am a beginner. How should I start UPSC preparation?
Start by reading
NCERT books (Class 6 to 12)
for History and Geography. Also, start reading a daily newspaper like 'The Hindu'.
How many hours should I study daily?
Consistency is key. Studying
6 to 8 hours daily
with full focus is enough to crack the exam.
Is it necessary to join coaching for IAS?
Self-study is possible, but coaching gives you a
structured plan, expert guidance, and a competitive environment
which speeds up your preparation.
How can I improve my answer writing skills?
Start writing one answer daily. At
CSMP Lucknow
, we check your answers every day and tell you how to improve.
Which newspaper is best for UPSC?
We recommend
The Hindu
or
The Indian Express
. Focus on the Editorial page and National news.
When should I start preparing for Optional Subject?
You should start your Optional subject preparation
3 months after
starting your GS preparation.
Is coaching available for working professionals?
Yes, we have a special
Weekend Batch (Saturday & Sunday)
and early morning batches for working people.
Can an average student crack the IAS exam?
Absolutely. UPSC looks for hard work and discipline, not just toppers. Many average students become IAS officers every year with the right guidance.
What is the 'Mentorship' program at CSMP?
Every student gets a
personal Mentor
. You can sit with your mentor 1-on-1 to discuss your stress, study plan, and weak areas.
How are doubts cleared?
You can ask doubts in the class. After class, teachers are
available for 30 minutes
. You can also message your mentor anytime.
Do you conduct Mock Interviews?
Yes, after you clear Mains, we provide
free Mock Interviews
with retired IAS/IPS officers to prepare you for the final stage.
Is the library facility available?
Yes, we have a quiet
Reading Room / Library
at our Gomti Nagar center open from
8 AM to 8 PM
for students.
Do you provide psychological support?
Yes, exam preparation is stressful. Our mentors act as a
support system
to keep you motivated and positive throughout the journey.
How do you track my progress?
We use a
Monthly Performance Report
. We track your test marks and attendance to see if you are improving or not.
Can I access the library on weekends?
Yes, the library is
open on Saturdays and Sundays
for self-study.
What happens if I fail to clear the exam this year?
We support our students until they succeed. You can
continue to use the library and consult mentors
even after your course ends.
```

## directors-desk

- URL: `/directors-desk/`
- Title: Director's Desk - CSMP IAS : India's Premier Coaching Institute for IAS / PCS
- Meta description: The journey to the Civil Services is one of the most demanding yet rewarding paths a student can take. When we established CSMP IAS in 2021, our goal was
- H1: Director’s Desk
- Body:

```
Director’s Desk
A Message from S.B. Shukla
Welcome to CSMP IAS.
The journey to the Civil Services is one of the most demanding yet rewarding paths a student can take. When we established CSMP IAS in 2021, our goal was clear: to bridge the gap between hard work and success through structured mentorship.
At CSMP IAS, we believe that an aspirant doesn’t just need information; they need a transformation. My journey as a mentor has shown me that with the right strategy, even the most complex subjects become manageable. Whether you are starting early with our “BA to Bureaucracy” program or refining your skills for the final interview, our commitment is to provide a home for your ambitions in the heart of Lucknow.
Our Success Stories
Since our inception in 2021, CSMP IAS has been proud to witness numerous aspirants turn their dreams into reality. Our success is reflected in the scores of students who have cleared the various stages of the Civil Services Examinations under our guidance. We celebrate every small win—from a student mastering their first answer-writing session to an aspirant securing their name in the final merit list. Your success is the true testimony of our hard work.
Our Vision
To be the most trusted catalyst in creating ethical, competent, and compassionate civil servants who are prepared to lead India into a brighter future. We envision an educational ecosystem where quality mentorship is accessible to every dedicated aspirant, regardless of their background.
Our Mission
Empowerment through Education:
To simplify the UPSC and UPPCS preparation process through innovative teaching and structured planning.
Early Foundation:
To nurture young minds through our integrated degree programs, ensuring they are “exam-ready” by the time they graduate.
Result-Oriented Mentorship:
To maintain a high success ratio by focusing on individual student performance rather than just completing the syllabus.
Our Approach
Our pedagogy is built on the
CSMP (Civil Services Mentorship Programme)
framework:
Personalized Mentorship:
Every student receives direct guidance from me to identify and overcome their specific academic hurdles.
Comprehensive Coverage:
From NCERT fundamentals to advanced GS papers, CSAT, and Essay writing, we cover every aspect of the syllabus.
The ‘BA to Bureaucracy’ Advantage:
A unique 3-year integrated approach that aligns university education with UPSC requirements.
Rigorous Testing:
Continuous evaluation through our specialized Prelims and Mains Test Series to build exam temperament.
Interview Mastery:
Personalized interview guidance sessions to refine the personality and communication skills of our students.
```

UPPCS – General Studies Foundation Course 2026–2027
The
General Studies Foundation Course (UPPCS 2026–27)
at
CSMP IAS Coaching, Lucknow
is a comprehensive and structured program designed to guide aspirants from basic understanding to advanced mastery. This course is built to provide the right direction, disciplined preparation, and consistent mentorship required to succeed in the UPPCS examination.
UPPCS is not just a competitive examination; it is a pathway to a career defined by responsibility, respect, and long-term stability. Keeping this in mind, this program ensures that every aspirant is equipped with clarity, strategy, and confidence throughout their preparation journey.
A Complete and Structured Preparation Program
This course is suitable for both beginners and serious aspirants. Whether you are starting from scratch or refining your preparation, the program follows a step-by-step approach from foundational concepts to advanced understanding.
The focus goes beyond syllabus completion. It emphasizes
concept clarity, answer writing improvement, and strategic preparation
to help students perform effectively in the examination.
Integrated Approach to Prelims and Mains
The course follows an integrated preparation model where both Prelims and Mains are prepared simultaneously. Students are trained to handle objective questions as well as develop structured and analytical answers for the Mains stage.
Regular answer writing practice and test-based learning ensure improvement in
accuracy, speed, and presentation
.
Supportive Learning Environment and Mentorship
At CSMP IAS, students are provided with a disciplined and motivating environment. Classes are organized according to the latest exam pattern, and each topic is covered with an exam-oriented approach.
Doubt resolution is prioritized, and continuous mentorship helps students stay consistent, focused, and confident throughout their preparation.
From Foundation to Advanced Level Mastery
For beginners, the course begins with NCERT-level concepts to build a strong base. Gradually, students are guided towards advanced topics and analytical thinking.
For experienced aspirants, the program focuses on improving
answer writing techniques, conceptual linking, and exam temperament
, which are essential for final selection.
UPPCS-Focused and Relevant Preparation
The course is specifically designed according to the UPPCS examination pattern. It includes
Uttar Pradesh-specific topics, current affairs, and previous year question analysis
.
This targeted approach ensures that preparation remains focused, relevant, and aligned with the actual demands of the examination.

Interview Guidance Program
Interview Guidance Program  | CSMP IAS Lucknow
Program Overview
Core Features
Personality Refining
Success Roadmap
Join the Elite
Interview Guidance Program (IGP) – CSMP IAS Lucknow
The final stage of the Civil Services Examination is not just a test of your knowledge, but a profound assessment of your personality, clarity of thought, and administrative potential. At
CSMP IAS Lucknow
, our
Interview Guidance Program (IGP)
is specifically designed to bridge the gap between being a candidate and becoming an officer. Under the direct supervision of
Dr. S.B. Shukla Sir
, we ensure that you walk into the UPSC/UPPCS interview board with unmatched confidence and poise.
The Philosophy of Our IGP
We believe that 'Personality' cannot be built overnight, but it can certainly be refined. Our program focuses on internalizing administrative traits such as integrity, emotional intelligence, and balanced decision-making. We don't just prepare you to answer questions; we prepare you to lead conversations.
Key Components of the Interview Program
Our IGP is recognized as one of the
most effective programs for final selection
due to its personalized nature:
Personalized DAF Analysis:
Detailed Application Form (DAF) is the base of your interview. Dr. S.B. Shukla Sir personally analyzes your DAF to identify potential questions related to your background, hobbies, and state.
One-on-One Mentorship:
Exclusive sittings with Dr. S.B. Shukla to work on your specific communication hurdles and body language.
Mock Interview Panels:
Real-time simulations with a panel of retired bureaucrats and subject experts to recreate the actual UPSC/UPPCS environment.
Current Affairs & Issue Analysis:
Special sessions to develop a balanced and administrative perspective on sensitive national and international issues.
Why Our IGP is Highly Effective for Students?
The transition from Mains to the Final Merit List depends heavily on the interview score. Our program is highly effective because:
Psychological Conditioning:
We help students overcome interview anxiety through repeated exposure and positive reinforcement.
Video Feedback Analysis:
Every mock interview is recorded, allowing students to observe their gestures, tone, and expressions for self-correction.
Niche Guidance:
Whether it is your first interview or your last attempt, our guidance is tailored to your level of experience.
Personality Refinement Pillars
We focus on the four essential pillars that the board looks for in a future bureaucrat:
Clarity of Expression:
Structuring your thoughts logically and concisely.
Poise and Posture:
Maintaining a calm and professional demeanor under pressure.
Intellectual Integrity:
Being honest and transparent in your responses.
Optimistic Outlook:
Demonstrating a problem-solving attitude toward socio-economic challenges.
Join the Final Leap to Success
Don't leave your final selection to chance. Join the experts at our
Gomti Nagar, Lucknow

Overview
COURSES
Strategy for Mains 2026

Syllabus in Details
UPSC Optional Subjects for Mains 2026
Choosing the right optional subject is one of the most important decisions in UPSC Civil Services preparation. Since candidates are allowed to select
only one optional subject
, this choice can significantly impact the final rank. At
CSMP IAS Lucknow
, we guide aspirants in understanding the UPSC Optional Subjects list, syllabus requirements, scoring potential, and preparation strategy to help them make an informed decision for the UPSC Mains Examination 2026.
How Many Optional Subjects Are There in UPSC?
UPSC provides a choice of
48 optional subjects
for the Civil Services Mains Examination. Out of these,
25 are core (non-literature) subjects
and
23 are literature subjects
. Candidates can choose
any one optional subject
, irrespective of their graduation background. Over the years, subjects like Geography, History, Sociology, Political Science & International Relations, Public Administration, and Anthropology have remained popular among aspirants due to syllabus overlap and availability of guidance.
List of UPSC Optional Subjects (Core Subjects)
The following optional subjects are available for the UPSC Mains Examination. CSMP IAS provides guidance and coaching support for selected optional subjects based on faculty expertise and student demand.
Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Science, Anthropology, Botany, Chemistry, Civil Engineering, Commerce and Accountancy, Economics, Electrical Engineering, Geography, Geology, History, Law, Management, Mathematics, Mechanical Engineering, Medical Science, Philosophy, Physics, Political Science and International Relations, Psychology, Public Administration, Sociology, Statistics, Zoology.
UPSC Literature Optional Subjects
Candidates can also choose literature of the following languages as their optional subject in the UPSC Mains Examination:
Assamese, Bengali, Bodo, Dogri, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Kashmiri, Konkani, Maithili, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Santhali, Sindhi, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, English.
Best Optional Subject for UPSC – How to Decide?
There is no single “best” optional subject for all candidates. Many IAS toppers have scored
320+ marks
in both technical and non-technical subjects. The key lies in choosing an optional subject that matches your background, interest, and preparation capacity. At CSMP IAS, mentors help aspirants evaluate optional subjects based on practical factors rather than trends alone.
Technical subjects such as Mathematics and Engineering are considered scoring due to objective answers, while humanities subjects offer better overlap with General Studies and Essay papers. The right optional subject is the one you can study consistently and confidently.
Key Questions to Ask Before Choosing an Optional Subject
Before finalizing an optional subject, aspirants should carefully consider the following:
How vast is the syllabus of the optional subject?
How much time can you realistically dedicate to optional preparation?
Do you have prior academic background or familiarity with the subject?
How much overlap does the optional have with GS Prelims and Mains syllabus?
Are coaching, study material, and guidance easily available?
Are you genuinely interested in studying the subject long-term?
CSMP IAS provides one-to-one counseling to help aspirants answer these questions and make the right choice.
Most Popular UPSC Optional Subjects
Based on past trends and student preferences, the following optional subjects are commonly chosen by UPSC aspirants:
Sociology, Public Administration, Geography, History, Political Science & International Relations, Anthropology, Law, Psychology, Agriculture, and Literature subjects.
Optional Subjects with High GS Syllabus Overlap
Some optional subjects overlap significantly with the General Studies syllabus, saving preparation time and improving answer quality:
Public Administration
– Strong overlap with GS Paper II (Polity & Governance).
Sociology
– Useful for GS Paper I, Essay, and Ethics Paper.
History
– Relevant for Prelims and GS Paper I.
Geography
– Helps in Prelims and GS Paper I.
Political Science & IR
– Useful for Prelims and GS Paper II.
Law
– Relevant for Prelims and GS Paper II.
Economics, Philosophy, and Agriculture are also good options depending on background and interest.
UPSC Optional Subjects – Success Rate (Reference Data)
Success rates vary across subjects and years. While some subjects show higher success ratios, CSMP IAS emphasizes that
answer quality, clarity, and consistency
matter more than statistics. A well-prepared candidate can score high in any optional subject with the right strategy and guidance.
How to Choose the Best UPSC Optional Subject – CSMP IAS Guidance
At CSMP IAS Lucknow, we help aspirants choose the right optional subject through academic counseling and strategic planning. Factors considered include syllabus length, overlap with GS, availability of resources, personal interest, and long-term consistency. Aspirants are advised not to select an optional solely based on toppers’ marks or popularity, as a wrong choice can cost an attempt.
UPSC Optional Subject Preparation Tips
Effective optional subject preparation requires a focused and disciplined approach:
Understand the syllabus thoroughly and use it as a checklist
Follow limited but standard study material and reliable sources
Practice answer writing regularly to improve structure and presentation
Attempt previous years’ question papers and mock tests
Revise topics weekly and monthly for better retention
Integrate current affairs wherever applicable to enrich answers
CSMP IAS provides structured optional coaching, study material, answer writing practice, and continuous evaluation to help aspirants master their optional subject for UPSC Mains.
CSMP IAS Lucknow – Expert Guidance for UPSC Optional Subject Selection & Preparation

General Studies Strategy for Mains 2026
GS Paper I Strategy
Focus is placed on linking history and geography with society and contemporary issues. Answers are enriched with examples, diagrams, and case studies wherever applicable.
GS Paper II Strategy
Special attention is given to polity, governance, and international relations. Students are trained to use constitutional articles, Supreme Court judgments, and current government initiatives in answers.
GS Paper III Strategy
Economic concepts, environment, disaster management, and internal security are covered with data, reports, and government schemes to improve answer quality.
GS Paper IV (Ethics) Strategy
Ethics preparation includes case study practice, value-based answers, and real-life examples. CSMP IAS helps aspirants develop clarity and ethical reasoning.
Optional Subject Strategy for Mains 2026
Since the optional subject carries
500 marks
, it plays a crucial role in final ranking. CSMP IAS provides structured optional subject preparation, including:
Complete syllabus coverage
Topic-wise answer writing
Previous years’ question analysis
Optional-specific test series
Students are guided to balance optional preparation with General Studies effectively.
Essay Paper Strategy
Essay writing is approached as a scoring opportunity. CSMP IAS trains students to develop coherent ideas, balanced arguments, and structured essays supported by facts, examples, and ethical perspectives.
Answer Writing & Evaluation
Regular answer writing practice is a core part of the CSMP IAS Mains strategy. Aspirants write answers under exam-like conditions and receive feedback on:
Content relevance
Structure and flow
Introduction and conclusion quality
Time management
Revision & Test Strategy
Revision is planned in multiple cycles to ensure retention. CSMP IAS conducts sectional tests, full-length Mains tests, and test discussions to help students identify gaps and improve continuously.

```
ESSAY Paper (UPPCS 2025)
नोट :
(i) प्रश्न-पत्र तीन खण्डों में विभाजित है। प्रत्येक खण्ड से केवल एक-एक विषय का चयन कर कुल तीन निबंध हिन्दी अथवा अंग्रेजी भाषा में लिखिए।
(ii) प्रत्येक निबंध में कुल प्रयुक्त शब्दों की अधिकतम सीमा 700 शब्दों की है।
(ii) प्रत्येक निबंध के लिए 50 अंक निर्धारित हैं।
Note:
(i) The question paper is divided into three sections. Write three essays in Hindi or English  language, selecting one topic from each section.
(ii) Maximum word limit of each Essay is 700.
(iii) Each essay carries 50 marks.
खंड – अ/SECTION – A
1. कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता के दौर में साहित्य का भविष्य ।
The future of literature in the age of Artificial Intelligence.
2. नए भारत की वैश्विक चेतना ।
Global consciousness of the New India.
3.इक्कीसवीं सदी में भारतीय स्त्री स्वप्न से यथार्थ तक ।
Indian women in the 21st century: From dreams to reality
खंड – ब/SECTION – B
4.विकास के निहितार्थ और पर्यावरण ।
The implications of development and the environment.
5.बदलती वैश्विक अर्थव्यवस्था में नैतिकता का प्रश्न ।
The issue of ethics in a changing global economy.
6.जैविक खेती: आवश्यकता या विवशता ।
Organic farming: Necessity or compulsion.
खंड – स/SECTION – C
7.भारत की विदेश नीति: गुटनिरपेक्षता से बहुध्रुवीय कूटनीति तक
India’s foreign policy: From non-alignment to multipolar diplomacy.
8.भूस्खलन: कितना मानवजनित कितना प्राकृतिक । Landslides:
How much Human-Induced, How much natural.
9.नए भारत का स्वप्न और ग्रामीण विकास योजनाएँ ।
The dream of New India Schemes. d Rural Development
```

- Body:

```
UPPCS मुख्य परीक्षा – 2025
सामान्य अध्ययन (प्रश्नपत्र – II)
GENERAL STUDIES (PAPER – II)
निर्धारित समय : तीन घण्टे                                                                                                    अधिकतम अंक : 200
Time Allowed : Three Hours                                                                                       Maximum Marks : 200
विशेष अनुदेश :
(i) कुल 20 प्रश्न दिए गये हैं। खण्ड(अ) में 10 प्रश्न लघु उत्तरीय हैं जिनके प्रत्येक उत्तर की शब्द-सीमा 125 तथा खण्ड(ब) में 10 प्रश्न दीर्घ उत्तरीय हैं जिनके प्रत्येक उत्तर की शब्द-सीमा 200 निर्धारित हैं। प्रश्न हिन्दी और अंग्रेजी दोनों में छपे हैं।
(ii) सभी प्रश्न अनिवार्य हैं।
(iii) प्रत्येक प्रश्न/भाग के लिए नियत अंक उसके सामने दिए गए हैं।
(iv) प्रश्नों में इंगित शब्द-सीमा को ध्यान में रखें।
(v) उत्तर पुस्तिका में खाली छोड़े गए कोई पृष्ठ अथवा पृष्ठ के भाग को पूर्णतः काट दें।
Specific Instructions :
(i) There are 20 questions. Section-A consists of 10 short answer questions with word limit of 125 each and Section-B consists of 10 long answer questions with word limit of 200 each. The questions are printed both in Hindi and in English.
(ii) All questions are compulsory.
(iii) The number of marks carried by a question/part is indicated against it.
(iv) Keep the word limit indicated in the questions in mind.
(v) Any page or portion of the page left blank in the answer booklet must be clearly struck off.
खण्ड – अ / SECTION – A
1. भारतीय विधायी प्रक्रिया में संयुक्त संसदीय समितियों (JPC) की क्या भूमिका है? वे प्रभावी कानून निर्माण में किस प्रकार योगदान देती हैं ? विश्लेषण कीजिए। 8
What role do Joint Parliamentary Committees (JPCs) play in the Indian legislative process? How do they contribute to effective law-making? Analyse.
2. वैकल्पिक विवाद समाधान (ADR) भारत में कुशल शासन को सुदृढ़ करने तथा न्याय वितरण प्रणाली की प्रभावशीलता बढ़ाने में किस प्रकार सहायक है? विश्लेषण कीजिए। 8
How does Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) strengthen efficient governance and enhance the effectiveness of the justice delivery system in India? Analyze.
3. “विधायिका अपने क्षेत्राधिकार में सर्वोच्च है, फिर भी वह संप्रभु नहीं है।” इस कथन का उदाहरणों सहित संवैधानिक परिप्रेक्ष्य में परीक्षण कीजिए। 8
“Legislature is supreme within its domain, yet it is not sovereign.” Examine this statement in the constitutional context with examples.
4. यह कहना कहाँ तक सही है कि अंतर-राज्य परिषद संघ तथा राज्यों के मध्य विवादों को प्रभावी ढंग से सुलझा सकती है? उपयुक्त उदाहरणों सहित उत्तर लिखिए। 8
To what extent is it correct to say that the Inter-State Council can effectively resolve the disputes between the Union and the States? Write the answer with suitable examples.
5. नागरिक-केन्द्रित प्रशासन को सुनिश्चित करने के लिए नागरिक चार्टर (प्राधिकार) एक ऐतिहासिक पहल रही है। टिप्पणी कीजिए। 8
The Citizen Charter has been a landmark initiative in ensuring citizen-centric administration. Comment.
6. भारत में मानव संसाधन विकास से संबंधित प्रमुख मुद्दों की व्याख्या कीजिए। 8 Explain the main issues relating to Human Resource Development in India.
7. नीति क्रियान्वयन में सूचना एवं संचार प्रौद्योगिकी (ICT), कहाँ तक उपयोगी रही है?विवेचना कीजिए। 8
To what extent has Information and Communication Technology (ICT) been useful in policy implementation? Discuss.
8.भारत – यूरोपियन यूनियन समझौते को वैश्विक भू-राजनीतिक गतिकी के परिवर्तनों के संदर्भ में कैसे देखा जाना चाहिए? स्पष्ट कीजिए। 8
How should the India – EU Agreement be viewed in the context of changing global geopolitical dynamics? Explain.
9. भारत की विदेश नीति के परिप्रेक्ष्य में श्रीलंका के भू-राजनीतिक महत्त्व का विश्लेषण कीजिए। Analyze the geopolitical significance of Sri Lanka in the context of India’s Foreign Policy. 8
10.सीमा-पार आतंकवाद पर भारत के दीर्घकालिक रुख की पुष्टि करने में 25वें शंघाई सहयोग संगठन (SCO) शिखर सम्मेलन, 2025 के घोषणा-पत्र के रणनीतिक महत्त्व का आकलन कीजिए। 8
Assess the strategic significance of the 25th Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit, 2025 Declaration, in endorsing India’s long-standing position on cross-border terrorism.
खण्ड – ब / SECTION – B
11.”भारत की संविधान निर्मात्री सभा औपनिवेशिक काल की संसदीय गतिविधियों का विधिक परिणाम थी।” इस कथन का आलोचनात्मक परीक्षण कीजिए। 12
“India’s Constituent Assembly was the legal outcome of Parliamentary developments during the Colonial period.” Critically examine this statement.
12.भारतीय संविधान के अंतर्गत संघ को प्रदान की गई विधायी शक्तियों का प्रावधान भारतीय संघीय प्रणाली के संघ-केंद्रित स्वरूप को किस प्रकार सुदृढ़ करता है? परीक्षण कीजिए। 12
How does the provision of legislative powers granted to the Union under the Indian Constitution contribute to the centralized character of India’s federal system? Examine.
13. “भारत का नियंत्रक एवं महालेखापरीक्षक (CAG) भारत के वित्त का सर्वोच्च पंच है।” इस कथन के आलोक में उसके कार्यों एवं स्थिति का आलोचनात्मक विश्लेषण कीजिए। 12
“The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is the supreme authority of India’s finance.” Critically analyse his functions and position in the light of this statement.
14.जनहित याचिका (PIL) सामाजिक न्याय को बढ़ावा देने एवं हाशिए पर पड़े समुदायों के अधिकारों की रक्षा करने का महत्त्वपूर्ण साधन है। उपयुक्त उदाहरणों सहित विश्लेषण कीजिए। 12
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is an important tool for promoting social justice and protecting the rights of marginalized communities. Analyse with suitable examples.
15.प्रत्यक्ष लाभ अंतरण (DBT) प्रणाली किस प्रकार डिजिटल इंडिया और सुशासन के उद्देश्यों के साथ मेल खाती है? विश्लेषण कीजिए। 12
How does the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) system align with the objectives of Digital India and good governance? Analyze.
16. ई-गवर्नेस के क्षेत्र में उभरते हुए आयामों का परीक्षण कीजिए तथा यह स्पष्ट कीजिए कि ये आयाम सरकारी सेवाओं को अधिक सुलभ, पारदर्शी और कुशल बनाने में किस प्रकार सहायक सिद्ध हो रहे हैं। 12
Examine the emerging dimensions of e-governance and explain how they contribute to making government services more accessible, transparent and efficient.
17. विकास प्रक्रिया में सहायक संस्थाओं, योगदानकर्ताओं (donors) तथा संस्थागत हितधारकों के मध्य समन्वय की आवश्यकता एवं व्यावहारिक वास्तविकताओं का समालोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन कीजिए। 12
Critically evaluate the need for coordination among support institutions, donors and institutional stakeholders in the development process and practical realities.
18. जम्मू-कश्मीर पुनर्गठन अधिनियम, 2019 की पृष्ठभूमि, प्रमुख प्रावधानों एवं इसके संवैधानिक, प्रशासनिक और राजनीतिक प्रभावों का समालोचनात्मक विश्लेषण कीजिए। 12
Critically analyze the background, key provisions and constitutional, administrative and political implications of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019.
19. “संयुक्त राष्ट्र सुरक्षा परिषद की संरचना समकालीन वैश्विक राजनीति की सत्यता को परिलक्षित नहीं करती है।” सुरक्षा परिषद के सुधार पर भारत के रुख के आलोक में इस कथन का आलोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन कीजिए। 12
“The structure of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) does not reflect the realities of contemporary global politics.” Critically evaluate this statement in the light of India’s stand on Security Council reforms.
20. भारत द्वारा विभिन्न देशों के साथ किए जा रहे मुक्त व्यापार समझौते (FTAs) किस सीमा तक भारत के निर्यात पर अमेरिकी (US) व्यापार नीतियों के प्रतिकूल प्रभावों को कम करने में सहायक हो सकते हैं ? इसका आलोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन कीजिए। 12
To what extent can India’s Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with various countries help mitigate the adverse effects of the US trade policies on India’s exports? Critically evaluate.
```

2. “नए विमानपत्तनों के निर्माण से भारत में औद्योगीकरण एवं विकास की राह आसान होगी।” परीक्षण कीजिए। 8
“Construction of new airports will facilitate industrialization and development in India.” Examine.
3. भारत में राष्ट्रीय प्रतिदर्श सर्वेक्षण कार्यालय (एन एस एस ओ) द्वारा विकसित बेरोज़गारी की अवधारणा पर चर्चा कीजिए। 8
Discuss the concept of unemployment in India as developed by National Sample Survey Office (NSSO).
4. डिजिटल भुगतान प्रणालियाँ भारत में वित्तीय समावेशन को कैसे बढ़ावा दे रही हैं?8
How are digital payment systems promoting financial inclusion in India?
5.”रोज़गारविहीन विकास”भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए एक बड़ी चिंता है।इस पृष्ठभूमि में, विनिर्माण क्षेत्र में”रोज़गार लोच की स्थिरता” के पीछे के कारणों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
“Jobless Growth” is a major concern for the Indian economy. In this backdrop, analyze the reasons behind the “stagnation of employment elasticity” in the manufacturing sector. 8
6. भारत में में समावेशी और सतत औद्योगीकरण (SDG 9) पर्यावरणीय स्थिरता (SDG 12,13) को सुनिश्चित करते हुए आर्थिक विकास (SDG 8) को कैसे बढ़ावा दे सकता है?
How can inclusive and sustainable industrialization (SDG 9) drive economic. growth (SDG 8), while ensuring environmental sustainability (SDG 12, 13) in India? 8
7. जैव-प्रौद्योगिकी में हुई हाल की प्रगति, विशेषकर जीनोम एडिटिंग, भारत की कृषि उत्पादकता और जलवायु-प्रतिरोध क्षमता को कैसे परिवर्तित कर रही है, इसका 2024-2025 के विशिष्ट उदाहरणों से परीक्षण कीजिए।
Examine how the recent developments in biotechnology, particularly genome editing, are reshaping India’s agricultural productivity and climate resilience, citing specific examples from 2024-2025. 8
8. सीमा-पार कट्टरपंथीकरण में सोशल मीडिया की भूमिका का मूल्यांकन कीजिए। 8
Evaluate the role of social media in radicalization across the borders.
9. “तमाम प्रयासों के बावजूद, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा हेतु ‘परमाणु प्रसार’ अभी भी एक चुनौती बना हुआ है।” इस कथन का आलोचनात्मक विश्लेषण कीजिए।
“Despite all efforts, Nuclear Proliferation’ still poses a challenge to international security.” Critically analyze this statement. 8
10. मानव तस्करी के प्रमुख कारणों की चर्चा करते हुए इससे पीड़ित व्यक्तियों की सुरक्षा एवं पुनर्वास में सरकार की भूमिका का उदाहरणों सहित वर्णन कीजिए।
Discuss the major causes of human trafficking and describe with examples, the role of the government in ensuring the protection and rehabilitation of the victims. 8
खण्ड – ब / SECTION – B
11. वर्षा और सिंचाई प्रणालियाँ एक-दूसरे की पूरक हैं, हैं, क्योंकि कृषि क्षेत्र मौसम की परिवर्तनशीलता के प्रति अत्यधिक संवेदनशील है। सहायक आँकड़ों के साथ इसकी पुष्टि कीजिए।
Rainfall and irrigation systems are complementary to each other as agriculture sector is highly vulnerable to weather eather variability. Justify with supportive data. 12
12. आय-असमानता से क्या तात्पर्य है? भारत में आय-असमानता को कैसे कम किया जा सकता है ?
What is meant by income inequality? How can income inequality be minimised in India? 12
13. वैश्विक आर्थिक तनावों एवं आयात-निर्यात संबंधी बाधाओं के भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था पर पड़ने वाले प्रभावों का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
Analyze the impact of global economic tensions and import-export obstacles on the Indian economy. 12
14. “स्वास्थ्य एवं शिक्षा में निवेश आर्थिक विकास का आधार है।” इस संदर्भ में भारत सरकार के विचारों को स्पष्ट कीजिए।
“Investment in health and education forms the foundation of economic development.” Explain the views of the Government of India in this context. 12
15. “भारत में भूमि सुधार एक अधूरा एजेंडा बना हुआ है।” व्याख्या कीजिए कि उचित भूमि अभिलेखों और काश्तकारी सुधारों की कमी भारत में कृषि के औद्योगीकरण और आधुनिकीकरण में बाधा के रूप में कैसे कार्य करती है।
“Land reforms in India remain an unfinished agenda.” Explain how the lack of proper land records and tenancy reforms act as hurdles in the industrialization and modernisation of agriculture in India. 12
16. भारत सरकार की स्टार्टअप योजना का प्रौद्योगिकी हस्तांतरण, आर्थिक विकास और भारत के सर्वांगीण विकास में योगदान का आकलन कीजिए।
Assess the contribution of Startup schemes of the Government of India in technology transfer, economic growth and overall development of India. 12
17. सूचना प्रौद्योगिकी, अंतरिक्ष प्रौद्योगिकी और जैव प्रौद्योगिकी भारत को एक विकसित राष्ट्र में परिवर्तित करने में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभा रहे हैं। उदाहरणों सहित विवेचना कीजिए।
Information technology, Space technology and Biotechnology are playing important roles in transforming India into a developed nation. Discuss with examples. 12
18. भारत की आंतरिक सुरक्षा के समक्ष मादक द्रव्य व संगठित अपराध किस प्रकार के खतरे हैं? इन चुनौतियों को नियंत्रित करने के लिए क्या उपाय किए जा सकते हैं?
What type of threats do drugs and organized crime pose to India’s internal security? What measures can be taken to control these challenges? 12
19. “सुरक्षा विकास है और विकास सुरक्षा है।”भारत की सुरक्षा के परिप्रेक्ष्य में इनके सहजीवी संबंध का विश्लेषण कीजिए।
“Security is development and developmen and development is security.” Analyze the symbiotic relationship from India’s security perspective. 12
20. औद्योगिक दुर्घटनाओं, आतंकी हमलों व आग जैसी मानव-निर्मित आपदाओं के जोखिम को कम करने के लिए कुछ प्रभावी रणनीतियाँ सुझाइए ।
Suggest some effective effective strategies for reducing the risk of man-made disasters like industrial accidents, terrorist attacks and fires. 12

- H1: UPPCS Mains – 2025
- Body:

```
UPPCS Mains – 2025
सामान्य अध्ययन (प्रश्न-पत्र I
)
GENERAL STUDIES (PAPER – I
)
निर्धारित समय : तीन घण्टे                                                                                                    अधिकतम अंक : 200
Time Allowed : Three Hours                                                                                       Maximum Marks : 200
विशेष अनुदेश :
(i) कुल 20 प्रश्न दिए गये हैं। खण्ड(अ) में 10 प्रश्न लघु उत्तरीय हैं जिनके प्रत्येक उत्तर की शब्द-सीमा 125 तथा खण्ड(ब) में 10 प्रश्न दीर्घ उत्तरीय हैं जिनके प्रत्येक उत्तर की शब्द-सीमा 200 निर्धारित हैं। प्रश्न हिन्दी और अंग्रेजी दोनों में छपे हैं।
(ii) सभी प्रश्न अनिवार्य हैं।
(iii) प्रत्येक प्रश्न/भाग के लिए नियत अंक उसके सामने दिए गए हैं।
(iv) प्रश्नों में इंगित शब्द-सीमा को ध्यान में रखें।
(v) उत्तर पुस्तिका में खाली छोड़े गए कोई पृष्ठ अथवा पृष्ठ के भाग को पूर्णतः काट दें।
Specific Instructions :
(i) There are 20 questions. Section-A consists of 10 short answer questions with word limit of 125 each and Section-B consists of 10 long answer questions with word limit of 200 each. The questions are printed both in Hindi and in English.
(ii) All questions are compulsory.
(iii) The number of marks carried by a question/part is indicated against it.
(iv) Keep the word limit indicated in the questions in mind.
(v) Any page or portion of the page left blank in the answer booklet must be clearly struck off.
1. मौर्य काल में कला एवं प्रौद्योगिकी के विकास पर एक संक्षिप्त टिप्पणी कीजिए । 8
Comment briefly on the development of art and technology during the Maurya period.
2. “उन्नसर्वी शताब्दी के भारतीय सामाजिक-धार्मिक सुधार आन्दोलनों में स्त्रीयों के मुद्दे एक प्रमुख चिंता का विषय थे” । स्पष्ट कीजिये । 8
“Women’s issue was a major concern in the socio-religious reform movements of 19th century India”. Explain.
3. ‘उग्रवाद उदारवादियों के विचारों और कार्य प्रणाली के विरुद्ध एक प्रतिक्रिया । एक प्रतिक्रिया थी’। इस कथन की आलोचनात्मक व्याख्या कीजिये । 8
‘Extremism was a reaction against the ideas and modus operandi of the moderates’. Critically explain this statement.
4. क्या वैश्वीकरण सांस्कृतिक एकीकरण एवं सांस्कृतिक संघर्ष दोनों को अग्रसर करता है? स्पष्ट कीजिए। 8
Does globalization leads to both cultural integration and cultural conflict? Elucidate.
5. ग्रामीण भारत में विकासात्मक मुद्दों के सन्दर्भ में निरक्षरता और गरीबी के बीच क्या सम्बन्ध है है ? आलोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन कीजिये । 8
What is the relationship between illiteracy and poverty in the context of developmental issu issues in rural India? Critically evaluate.
6. आधुनिक भारत में क्षेत्रवाद चुनौती एवं अवसर दोनों है। स्पष्ट कीजिए । 8
Regionalism in modern India is both a challenge and an opportunity. Clarify.
7. भारत में हिमनदों की प्रकृति में विभिन्नताओं की समीक्षा कीजिये। 8
Examine the variations in nature of glaciers in India.
8. भारत में मैंग्रोव और प्रवाल भित्ति समुद्री संसाधन प्रबन्धन में किस प्रकार योगदान प्रदान करते हैं ? 8
How do India’s mangroves and corals reefs contribute to marine resource management?
9. चीन-भारत सीमा विवाद के उद्भव, विस्तार और निहितार्थ का परीक्षण कीजिये।8 Examine the origin, dimensions and implications of Sino-Indian border dispute.
10. मानसून की उत्पत्ति के अभिनव सिद्धान्तों का आलोचनात्मक परीक्षण कीजिये तथा मानसून पर एल-निनो के प्रभावों का विवेचन कीजिये । 8
Examine critically the recent theories of the origin of monsoon and discuss the effects of El-nino on monsoon.
11. स्वतन्त्रता पश्चात् भारत के एकीकरण में सरदार पटेल की भूमिका का आलोचनात्मक विश्लेषण कीजिए। 12
Critically analyse the role of Sardar Patel in the Unification of India after Independence.
12. “1857 से 1947 का कालखण्ड भारत के इतिहास का अत्यधिक परिवर्तन का काल था”। इस कथन का विश्लेषण कीजिए ।
“The period from 1857 to 1947 was a time of immense change of Indian history”. Analyse this statement
13. जर्मनी का एकीकरण ‘राष्ट्रवाद के आदर्श’ और ‘यथार्थवादी शक्ति-राजनीति’ के अंतर्विरोध का प्रतीक माना जाता है। इस सन्दर्भ में एकीकरण के मागों और उसके और उसके अंतरर्राष्ट्रीय निहितार्थों का आलोचनात्मक परीक्षण कीजिए । 12
The Unification of Germany is considered as a symbol of the contradiction between the ‘ideal of nationalism’ and the ‘realities of power politics’. In this context, critically examine the paths of unification and its international implications.
14. नगरीकरण से संबद्ध समाजिक-आर्थिक समस्याओं की विवेचना कीजिए। सतत शहरी विकास हेतु कौन-से संरचनात्मक उपाय आवश्यक है ? 12
Discuss the socio-economic problems associated with urbanization. What structural measures are necessary for sustainable urban development?
15. भारतीय परम्परागत मूल्यों पर आधुनिकीकरण एवं पश्चिमीकरण के प्रभावों का आलोचनात्मक मूल्यांकन कीजिये । 12
Critically evaluate the impact of modernisation and westernisation on the traditional Indian values.
16. परिवार, विवाह एवं नातेदारी व्यवस्था पर वैश्वीकरण का क्या प्रभाव दिखाई देता हैं ? भारतीय समाज के सन्दर्भ में इसका विश्लेषण कीजिए । 12
What are the visible effects of globalization on family, marriage and kinship system? Analyse with reference to the Indian society.
17. ‘भारत के वन संसाधनों का परीक्षण कीजिये तथा उन संरक्षण सिद्धान्तों को समझाइये जो देश की वन सम्पदा के विकास में प्रयुक्त किये जा सकते है। 12
Examine the forest resources of India and explain the principles of conservation which could be applied to improve the forest wealth of India.
18. शरणार्थियों एवं घुसपैठियों में भेद कीजिए। शरणार्थियों की सुरक्षा और सहायता के लिए भारत सरकार ने कौन-से कदम उठाये है? 12
Differentiate between refugees and infiltrators.What steps have been taken by the Government of India for the security and assistance of refugees?
19. “भारत का महाद्वीपीय मग्नतट खनिज और ऊर्जा का भण्डार है”। उपयुक्त उदाहरणों के साथ इस कथन का आलोचनात्मक परीक्षण कीजिये। 12
“India’s continental shelf is a store house of mineral and energy resources”. Critically examine this statement with suitable examples.
20. सीमान्त और सीमाओं में अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिये और भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप से उपयुक्त उदाहरण देते हुये सीमाओं के प्रकारों पर विस्तृत विवरण प्रस्तुत कीजिये। 12
Differentiate between frontiers and boundaries and present a detailed account on the types of examples from Indian subcontinent. giving suitable.
```

```
UPPCS Hindi Paper 2025
Marks: 150
Time Duration: 3hrs
विशेष अनुदेश / SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS
नोट:
(i) सभी प्रश्न अनिवार्य हैं।
(ii) प्रत्येक प्रश्न के अंत में निर्धारित अंक अंकित हैं।
(iii) पत्र, प्रार्थना पत्र या किसी अन्य प्रश्न के उत्तर के साथ अपना अथवा अन्य किसी का नाम, पता (प्रश्न-पत्र में दिए गए नाम, पदनाम आदि को छोड़कर) एवं अनुक्रमांक न लिखें। आवश्यक होने पर क, ख, ग का उल्लेख कर सकते हैं।
Note:
(i) All questions are compulsory.
(ii) Marks are given against each of the question.
(iii) Do not write your or another’s name, address (excluding those name, designation etc. given in the question paper) and roll no. with letter, application or any other question. You can mention क, ख, ग if necessary.
निम्नलिखित गद्यांश के आधार पर नीचे लिखे प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
भारतीय समाज की शक्ति का स्रोत उसका पारिवारिक जीवन है। अनेक परिवर्धनों के बीच में परिवार की यह दृढ़ शक्ति बारंबार उभरती हुई दिखाई पड़ती है। परिवार की इस शक्ति का विघटन किसी भी प्रकार समाज के लिए हितकारी नहीं हो सकता। भारतीय-परिवार सामाजिक जीवन के क्षेत्र में मूल्यवान प्रयोग है, उसे सब तरह से बढ़ाना, पल्लवित और पुष्पित करना आवश्यक है। आजकल के संक्रांति काल में तो परिवार के संगठन को और भी सुसंस्कृत करना आवश्यक है। कुल-संस्कृति का महत्त्वपूर्ण ग्रंथ ‘रामायण’ है। जैसे भारतीय संस्कृति का प्रतीक कुल है, वैसे ही भारतीय साहित्य की विशिष्ट कृति ‘रामायण’ है। धर्म तत्त्व परिवार के प्रत्येक सदस्य के समक्ष कर्तव्य का संदेश लाता है। माता-पिता, पति-पत्नी, पुत्र-पुत्री, भाई-बहन, जाति-बंधु, जिनका परिवार से नाता होता है, वे सब कर्तव्य के ऋण से बँधे होते हैं। कर्तव्य द्वारा व्यक्ति सेवा का मार्ग अपनाता है। कर्तव्य-भावना का ही दूसरा नाम यज्ञीय भावना है। जहाँ व्यक्ति दूसरे के लिए अपने स्वार्थ और सुख का समर्पण करता है, उस जीवन को स्वर्ग कहते हैं। महान् ग्रंथ जो आदर्श सिखाते हैं, उनकी भावना यही है।
परिवार के प्रेममय वातावरण में सब सदस्य अपने कर्तव्य को पहचानकर उसका पालन करते हैं। दूसरों से छीन-झपटकर अपने लिए कुछ प्राप्त करने की बात वे मन में नहीं लाते। यही पारिवारिक जीवन का रस है। जहाँ एक व्यक्ति दूसरे की सहायता और सेवा करने की बात सोचता है, वही आदर्श स्थिति स्वर्ग है। इसके विपरीत जब हम प्रत्येक वस्तु को अपने स्वार्थ की दृष्टि से देखते हैं और अधिकार की बात कहकर केवल पाने या लेने की इच्छा रखते हैं, तो हमारे उस आचरण से संघर्ष और विरोध उत्पन्न हो जाता है। उस तनाव की स्थिति में जो न हो जाए, थोड़ा है।

निम्नलिखित गद्यांश के आधार पर नीचे लिखे प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।
गरीबी हमारा मानसिक रोग है। यदि आप इस रोग से पीड़ित हैं अथवा इस रोग के शिकार हैं, तो अपने मानसिक भाव को बदल दीजिए। दुःख-दरिद्रता तथा लाचारी के विचार मन में लाने के स्थान पर सुख-समृद्धि, ऐश्वर्य, स्वाधीनता तथा आनंद के विचारों से अपने मानस-क्षेत्र को प्रकाशित कीजिए। फिर यह देखकर आपके आश्चर्य का पार न रहेगा कि आपकी उन्नति कितने जोरों से हो रही है।
हमें विजय और सफलता पूर्णतया मन की वैज्ञानिक प्रक्रिया से प्राप्त होती है। जो मनुष्य समृद्धिशाली और सौभाग्यशाली होता है उसका यह अखण्ड विश्वास होता है कि वह संमृद्धिशाली और सौभाग्यशाली हो रहा है। उसे अपनी कमाने की योग्यता पर विश्वास रहता है। वह अपने समय को गरीबी की बातों तथा विचारों में नहीं गँवाता। दरिद्रता से लड़खड़ाता हुआ नहीं चलता। वह अपनी शक्ति को उस वस्तु की ओर मोड़ता है, जिसके लिए कोशिश कर रहा है तथा जिसकी प्राप्ति में उसका पूरा विश्वास एवं दृढ़ निश्चय है।
देश में ऐसे गरीब लोग हैं, जो अपनी गरीबी से अर्ध-संतुष्ट हो गए हैं और जिन्होंने उसके विकराल पंजों से निकलने का प्रयत्न ही छोड़ दिया है। अब वे चाहे कितना ही कठिन परिश्रम करें, उन्होंने तो अपनी आशा खो दी है – स्वाधीनता प्राप्त करने की उमंग नष्ट कर दी है।

## complete-strategy-guide-for-working-professionals

```
PCS with Job: Complete Strategy Guide for Working Professionals | CSMP IAS 12-Month Roadmap
CSMP IAS • PCS Preparation Series
PCS with Job: How Working Professionals Can Crack PCS Without Quitting Their Career
A realistic, field-tested strategy for aspirants who want to clear UPPCS / State PCS examinations while continuing their government or private job — plus CSMP IAS’s structured 12-month roadmap.Complete Strategy Guide for Working Professionals
60%+PCS aspirants are working professionals
3–4 hrsDaily study needed on average
12Months in CSMP IAS roadmap
2Stages: Prelims + Mains preparation tracks
Every year, lakhs of candidates appear for the Provincial Civil Services (PCS) examination conducted by state Public Service Commissions such as UPPSC, BPSC, MPPSC, and others. What most coaching advertisements don’t tell you is a simple truth: a large share of successful PCS candidates were not full-time students sitting in a library for twelve hours a day. They were teachers, bank employees, government clerks, private-sector professionals, and even those managing family businesses — people who cracked PCS
while holding a job
.
If you are one of these working aspirants, this guide is written specifically for you. We will walk through why PCS-with-job is absolutely achievable, how to structure your limited hours for maximum output, which mistakes derail working aspirants most often, and finally, we’ll lay out the
CSMP IAS 12-month roadmap
— a month-by-month plan designed around the reality of a working professional’s schedule rather than the fantasy of unlimited study time.
The Core Truth
PCS is not won by the person who studies the most hours. It is won by the person who studies the
right
material, revises it enough times, and stays consistent for the full 10–12 months without burning out. A working aspirant with 3.5 focused hours daily will comfortably outperform a full-time aspirant who studies 8 distracted hours.
1. Is It Really Possible to Crack PCS with a Job?
Yes — and the exam’s own structure supports this. PCS Prelims is a screening-based objective test covering General Studies and (in most states) CSAT as qualifying. It rewards conceptual clarity, static-plus-current-affairs revision, and smart practice — not raw hours. Mains, similarly, rewards structured answer-writing and command over a manageable optional subject rather than encyclopedic knowledge. Complete Strategy Guide for Working Professionals The one liner answer is YES its completely possible for those who are working somewhere   Working Professionals Can Crack PCS Without Quitting Their Career
The real challenge for a working aspirant is not intelligence or aptitude. It is
time fragmentation
— study happening in scattered 45-minute blocks around office hours, commute, and family responsibilities. The entire strategy below is built to solve exactly this problem.
Who Typically Succeeds in the Job + PCS Combination
1
Government employees
Clerks, teachers, and Group C/D staff already familiar with exam culture and syllabus overlap with other government exams.
2
Private sector professionals
IT, banking, or corporate employees who bring strong time-management and analytical habits from their jobs.
3
Teachers and tutors
Already engaged with GS-adjacent subjects; can integrate revision into their teaching schedule.
4
Contractual/part-time workers
Often have more flexible hours, allowing longer uninterrupted study blocks on certain days.
2. Building a Realistic Daily Schedule
Forget the 10-hour study charts circulating on social media — they are written for full-time aspirants and will only generate guilt in a working professional. Instead, build a schedule around your actual job timings. Below is a sample structure assuming a standard 9-to-6 job.
Time Slot
Duration
Activity
5:30 AM – 7:00 AM
1.5 hrs
Deep-focus study: static GS or optional subject (fresh mind, best for new concepts)
Commute (to/from office)
45–60 min
Current affairs audio notes, revision via mobile app, or MCQ practice
Lunch break at office
20–30 min
Quick revision of static notes or one editorial reading
9:00 PM – 11:00 PM
2 hrs
Answer writing (Mains phase) or MCQ practice + error analysis (Prelims phase)
Weekly (Sat/Sun)
6–8 hrs/day
Full-length mock tests, weekly revision, current affairs compilation, doubt clearing
This adds up to roughly
4–4.5 hours on weekdays
and
6–8 hours on weekends
— a sustainable 30–35 hours per week, which is entirely sufficient if maintained consistently across 10–12 months.
Pro Tip
Protect your early morning slot fiercely. It is the only time of day a working aspirant has genuine control over — no meetings, no calls, no family demands. Whatever you study in that window should be the hardest, highest-priority material of the day.
3. Subject-Wise Prioritisation for Limited Time
With limited hours, you cannot treat every subject with equal depth. CSMP IAS recommends a tiered approach:
Tier 1 — High Weightage, Must Master
Indian Polity and Governance
Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
State-specific History, Geography, and Culture (critical for state PCS)
Current Affairs (last 12 months, integrated with static topics)
Tier 2 — Moderate Weightage, Build Working Knowledge
Indian and World Geography
Economy and Government Schemes
Environment and Ecology
Science and Technology (application-based, not rote)
Tier 3 — Selective Depth
Ancient and Medieval History (focus on state-relevant portions)
Art and Culture
Ethics (for Mains, where applicable)
A working aspirant should spend roughly 60% of study time on Tier 1, 30% on Tier 2, and 10% on Tier 3 during the early months, gradually rebalancing toward full-syllabus revision as the exam approaches.
4. Prelims Strategy for Working Aspirants
Prelims is the biggest filter in PCS and demands speed, accuracy, and elimination technique — all trainable even in limited time.
One standard source per subject
— resist the temptation to collect multiple books. Multiplicity of sources is the single biggest time-waster for working aspirants.
Daily MCQ practice
— even 20–25 questions daily during commute builds pattern recognition over months.
Monthly current affairs compilation
— rather than daily newspaper reading (often unrealistic for working people), use a trusted monthly compilation supplemented by weekly headline scanning.
Weekend full-length mocks
— simulate exam-day conditions at least twice a month from month 6 onward.
Negative marking discipline
— analyse every mock to identify guesswork-driven errors versus knowledge gaps.
5. Mains Strategy: Answer Writing on a Tight Schedule
Mains is where most working aspirants lose ground — not due to lack of knowledge, but lack of practice writing structured answers under time pressure.
Start answer writing early
— ideally from month 4–5, not after Prelims results. Waiting until after Prelims leaves too little runway.
Two answers a day is enough
— quality and structured feedback matter more than volume.
Choose your optional subject strategically
— pick a scoring, well-resourced optional with syllabus overlap with GS wherever possible (Public Administration, Sociology, and Geography are common choices for working aspirants due to conceptual and current-affairs overlap).
Build a Mains value-addition register
— a running notebook of quotes, data points, committee reports, and diagrams to be sprinkled across answers.
Common Trap
Do not attempt to “finish the syllabus first, then start writing.” Syllabus completion and answer-writing practice must run in parallel from the mid-point of your preparation — otherwise you will face the syllabus in full only weeks before Mains, with no writing practice behind you.
6. Managing Current Affairs Without Burning Out
Current affairs is the most time-hungry component of PCS preparation and the easiest to over-invest in. For working aspirants, CSMP IAS recommends:
One reliable monthly magazine or compilation instead of daily newspaper cutting.
A weekly 45-minute “current affairs Sunday” session to consolidate the week’s static-current linkages.
State-specific current affairs given separate, dedicated attention — this is frequently under-prepared by candidates who over-focus on national news.
Integration technique: whenever you study a static topic (say, Panchayati Raj), immediately note any related current development, rather than treating the two as separate study streams.Home | UPPSC, Prayagraj
7. The Seven Mistakes That Derail Working Aspirants
1
Over-ambitious daily targets
Planning 6 hours on weekdays and failing repeatedly, which erodes motivation faster than a modest, achievable plan.
2
Source hopping
Switching books or coaching notes every few months instead of revising the same material multiple times.
3
Delaying answer writing
Treating Mains preparation as a “later problem” until after the Prelims result is out.
4
Ignoring revision cycles
Moving forward in the syllabus without scheduled revision, leading to forgetting what was studied months earlier.
5
No mock test discipline
Skipping weekend mocks due to fatigue, which removes the only real exam-simulation practice available.
6
Guilt-driven burnout
Comparing progress with full-time aspirants and overcompensating with unsustainable study binges.
7
No leave planning near exam dates
Failing to plan office leave in advance for the final revision weeks before Prelims and Mains.
8. CSMP IAS 12-Month Roadmap for PCS Aspirants with a Job
This roadmap assumes a working aspirant starting from zero to moderate preparation level, targeting the next PCS cycle. Adjust the timeline slightly depending on your exact exam calendar and current stage of preparation.
Month 1 – Foundation & Syllabus Mapping
Understand the complete Prelims and Mains syllabus, state-specific exam pattern, and previous 5 years’ question trends. Select standard NCERT/state board books for Polity, History, and Geography. Set up your daily and weekend schedule. Begin Tier 1 subjects.
Month 2 – Polity & Modern History Core
Complete Indian Polity fundamentals (Constitution, governance structures, amendments) and Modern History (freedom struggle, key movements). Begin daily 20-question MCQ practice during commute.
Month 3 – Geography & State-Specific Content
Cover Indian and state geography in depth — this is disproportionately important for state PCS. Start building a state current affairs file alongside national current affairs.
Month 4 – Economy, Environment & Optional Subject Selection
Cover economy basics and government schemes, plus environment and ecology. Finalise your Mains optional subject based on interest, scoring history, and resource availability. Begin optional subject syllabus.
Home | UPPSC, Prayagraj
Month 5 – Answer Writing Begins
Start writing two GS answers daily alongside continued syllabus coverage. Begin first full revision cycle of Months 1–4 material on weekends.
Month 6 – Science, Tech & First Full-Length Prelims Mock
Cover Science and Technology (applied, current-affairs linked). Take your first full-length Prelims mock test and conduct detailed error analysis. Continue optional subject and answer writing.
Month 7 – Revision Cycle 2 + Current Affairs Consolidation
Second full revision of static syllabus. Consolidate 6 months of current affairs into a compact revision file. Increase weekend mock frequency to twice a month.
Month 8 – Optional Subject Depth + Ethics (if applicable)
Deepen optional subject preparation with past-year answer writing. Cover Ethics/Aptitude portions if part of your state’s Mains pattern. Continue mock test cycle.
Month 9 – Prelims Intensive Phase
Shift primary focus to Prelims: daily MCQ sets, weekly full mocks, and rapid revision of all static subjects using notes rather than original books. Reduce optional subject hours temporarily.
Month 10 – Final Prelims Push (Pre-Exam Month)
Plan office leave for the final 7–10 days before Prelims. Focus exclusively on revision, mock analysis, and current affairs recap. Avoid starting any new topic this month.
Month 11 – Prelims Exam & Mains Transition
Appear for Prelims. Immediately transition into Mains mode within a week regardless of expected result — resume optional subject depth and intensive answer writing practice, since the Mains window is typically short.
Month 12 – Mains Intensive & Final Revision
Full-length Mains mocks under timed conditions, value-addition register revision, and structured essay practice. Plan extended office leave for the final two weeks before Mains for uninterrupted preparation.
How CSMP IAS Supports This Roadmap
CSMP IAS structures its PCS batches specifically around this working-aspirant timeline — with recorded lectures for flexible viewing, weekend-focused doubt sessions, monthly current affairs compilations, and a dedicated answer-writing evaluation track so that Mains practice doesn’t get postponed.
9. Frequently Asked Questions
Q1. How many hours are really enough to crack PCS while working?
3.5 to 4.5 focused hours on weekdays, combined with 6–8 hours on weekends, is generally sufficient across a 10–12 month timeline — provided the study is structured and revision cycles are maintained.
Q2. Should I take a break from my job closer to the exam?
Most successful working aspirants take planned leave only for the final 7–10 days before Prelims and the final two weeks before Mains, rather than resigning or taking extended leave for the entire preparation period.
Q3. Which optional subject is best for working PCS aspirants?
Subjects with syllabus overlap with GS and easy availability of standard material — such as Public Administration, Sociology, or Geography — tend to work well since they reduce the total independent study burden.
Q4. Is coaching necessary for working aspirants?
Not mandatory, but structured guidance — through recorded lectures, test series, and answer evaluation — saves significant time by removing the need to independently curate sources and validate answer quality, which is especially valuable when study hours are limited.
Q5. What if I miss a day or fall behind the schedule?
Build a buffer day into your weekly plan (commonly Sunday evening) specifically to absorb missed targets, rather than trying to compress two days of material into one — this prevents the cascading burnout that ends many working aspirants’ attempts.
Conclusion
Cracking PCS while holding a job is not a compromise strategy — it is a legitimate, well-trodden path followed by a majority of successful candidates every year. The difference between those who succeed and those who don’t is rarely talent. It is
structure, consistency, and realistic planning
sustained over 10–12 months. With a disciplined daily schedule, tiered subject prioritisation, early answer-writing practice, and a clear roadmap like the one outlined above, a working professional is fully capable of clearing PCS without walking away from their career.
Start Your PCS Journey with CSMP IAS
Join CSMP IAS’s dedicated PCS-with-Job batch — structured around working professionals’ schedules, with recorded lectures, weekend doubt sessions, and evaluated answer writing.
Explore CSMP IAS PCS Batch
Election Commission of India: A Complete Guide for UPSC Aspirants 2026
© 2026 CSMP IAS. This article is for educational guidance purposes for PCS aspirants.
```
